samples.summary: Font-readiness assertion is still vacuous when the Google Fonts stylesheet itself fails to load
samples.evidence: The todo doc for this change (docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:75-76) claims the new per-family "at least one face reached loaded" assertion "is what makes an unreachable CDN fail rather than pass". But the awaited set is derived *entirely* from `document.fonts` (registry(), line 385-396), and every face in this app comes from remote stylesheets (packages/frontend/index.html:12 and font-catalog.ts:103 — grep found no local `@font-face` in packages/frontend). If the css2 stylesheet request itself fails/is blocked (404/429/no network/DNS), no `@font-face` rules exist, so `registry()` is empty, `pending()` iterates nothing and returns `[]`, and `settlePass` reports success. Capture then proceeds with fallback glyphs, `webFontFailures` stays empty, and the new `if (updateBaseline && webFontFailures.length > 0)` guard at line ~624 ("Refusing to record baselines from fallback glyphs") never fires — i.e. the guard is vacuous in exactly the scenario it advertises. `refetchPass` has the same hole: with zero matching links it rewrites nothing and returns 0, which the caller ignores. The harness's own assertion therefore passes independently of whether the behavior it checks (usable webfonts) holds.

samples.summary: No floor of expected families/weights: nothing asserts the fonts the baselines were recorded with are actually present
samples.evidence: The previous code kept an explicit `VISUAL_FONT_FAMILIES`/`VISUAL_FONT_WEIGHTS` floor; the diff deletes it and derives everything from the page registry, with the comment "the wait cannot drift from them". There is now no assertion anywhere that Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono (the families the baselines were recorded against, index.html:12) were registered at all — the very families whose absence caused the original slides-theme-panel / slides-pickers drift documented in the todo. A minimal non-derived expectation (e.g. `Inter` must appear in the registry with a `loaded` face) is what would keep the check from passing on an empty registry. Searched: whole script for any hard-coded family/weight list, `grep` for VISUAL_FONT_FAMILIES / expected fonts across the repo, packages/frontend/tests for visual-harness font assertions.

samples.summary: New failure/deferral semantics (record-and-continue, refuse update, deferred exit 1) have no automated test
samples.evidence: The diff adds non-trivial control flow that is pure orchestration policy: `webFontRefetchExhausted` short-circuiting later passes, `webFontFailures` accumulation, refusing `--update` when failures exist, and a deferred `process.exit(1)` after diffs are written. None of it is exercised by any test: the script is a top-level side-effecting module with everything inline in closures and nothing exported, so it cannot even be imported for a unit test. The repo does unit-test comparable script logic elsewhere (scripts/agent/*.test.mjs, scripts/test/verify-entropy.test.mjs), so the pattern exists; extracting the failure-bookkeeping/exit-decision into a testable pure helper would let these paths be asserted. Searched: glob packages/frontend/scripts/** (no test files), grep for 'verify-visual-browser' (only package.json, docker script, docs), glob **/*.test.mjs (none under packages/frontend).

samples.summary: Per-family 'one loaded face' bar can report a false failure for registered-but-unpainted families
samples.evidence: `pending()` fails any registered family with no `loaded` face. A lazily injected per-family link (useGoogleFontsLink / docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:346) registers faces even when no visible text in the captured section uses that family, and Chromium only fetches a face once text using it is laid out — so such a family can legitimately stay `unloaded` for the whole 10s deadline, burn both refetch attempts, set `webFontRefetchExhausted`, and record a `webFontFailures` entry that makes the run exit 1 with correct pixels. This would make the harness's own gate unreliable (flaky red) rather than inadequate; flagging as the test-infrastructure trust concern, deferring the correctness detail to that lens.

finding.summary: Font-readiness assertion is still vacuous when the Google Fonts stylesheet itself fails to load
finding.evidence: The todo doc for this change (docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:75-76) claims the new per-family "at least one face reached loaded" assertion "is what makes an unreachable CDN fail rather than pass". But the awaited set is derived *entirely* from `document.fonts` (registry(), line 385-396), and every face in this app comes from remote stylesheets (packages/frontend/index.html:12 and font-catalog.ts:103 — grep found no local `@font-face` in packages/frontend). If the css2 stylesheet request itself fails/is blocked (404/429/no network/DNS), no `@font-face` rules exist, so `registry()` is empty, `pending()` iterates nothing and returns `[]`, and `settlePass` reports success. Capture then proceeds with fallback glyphs, `webFontFailures` stays empty, and the new `if (updateBaseline && webFontFailures.length > 0)` guard at line ~624 ("Refusing to record baselines from fallback glyphs") never fires — i.e. the guard is vacuous in exactly the scenario it advertises. `refetchPass` has the same hole: with zero matching links it rewrites nothing and returns 0, which the caller ignores. verdict.reason: The described code exists exactly as claimed and is reachable. `registry()` (verify-visual-browser.mjs:385-396) derives the awaited set solely from `document.fonts`; `pending()` (:415-439) iterates that map, so an empty registry yields `[]`, `settlePass` returns `[]` (:450-457) and `waitForFontsReady` returns success (:480-486) without pushing to `webFontFailures` (only pushed at :490 when `pending.length > 0`). Every face in this app comes from remote css2 stylesheets (index.html:12, font-catalog.ts:103); a repo-wide grep found no local `@font-face` rules or `new FontFace`/`document.fonts.add` in packages/frontend, so a blocked/404 stylesheet leaves the registry empty and the assertion passes vacuously. `refetchPass` (:463-473) matches zero links in that state and its return value is discarded at the call site (:496). Consequently the advertised guard at :640-645 ("Refusing to record baselines from fallback glyphs") can never fire in the very scenario the todo doc (docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:75-76, :89-92) says it covers, meaning `visual:update` would record fallback-glyph baselines. No guard elsewhere rescues it: the script has no requestfailed/response-status check (that exists only in the unrelated hunt-ui-oracles.mjs:150), no non-empty-registry sanity check, and no test anywhere exercises waitForFontsReady/settlePass. This is in-lane fake coverage (an assertion true regardless of the behavior it claims to check), major impact.

finding.summary: No floor of expected families/weights: nothing asserts the fonts the baselines were recorded with are actually present
finding.evidence: The previous code kept an explicit `VISUAL_FONT_FAMILIES`/`VISUAL_FONT_WEIGHTS` floor; the diff deletes it and derives everything from the page registry, with the comment "the wait cannot drift from them". There is now no assertion anywhere that Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono (the families the baselines were recorded against, index.html:12) were registered at all — the very families whose absence caused the original slides-theme-panel / slides-pickers drift documented in the todo. A minimal non-derived expectation (e.g. `Inter` must appear in the registry with a `loaded` face) is what would keep the check from passing on an empty registry. Searched: whole script for any hard-coded family/weight list, `grep` for VISUAL_FONT_FAMILIES / expected fonts across the repo, packages/frontend/tests for visual-harness font assertions.

verdict.reason: The reviewer is right that no hard-coded Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono floor exists (I grepped repo-wide for REQUIRED_FONT|EXPECTED_FONT|FONT_FAMILIES|expectedFamilies and read the harness page/scenarios), but the conclusion "nothing asserts the fonts the baselines were recorded with are actually present" is wrong: the lane's actual assertion is the baseline pixel comparison. verify-visual-browser.mjs:692-723 diffs every capture against its recorded baseline with a tight budget (ratio 0.0001 / floor 20 px, :165-179) and :746-752 exits non-zero on any mismatch. Inter is the app's body family (index.html:12) and the heading font of several built-in slides themes, so a capture taken with an empty font registry paints fallback glyphs and fails — which is exactly how the drift in the referenced todo was caught (docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:5-18: slides-theme-panel 339 px, slides-pickers 818 px, detected by pixel diff alone with no family floor in play). The vacuous-check case the finding worries about (fonts.check() true for an unregistered family) is separately guarded inside the script by the per-family "at least one face reached loaded" assertion (:415-427), with refetch/report (:476-497) and a refusal to record baselines from fallback glyphs (:640-645). So the coverage is not fake: missing baseline fonts still fail the run loudly with artifacts. The only residual hole — recording brand-new baselines in an environment where the fonts stylesheet request fails entirely — is documented as a known limitation (todo:87-92) and self-corrects on the next comparison run; it is a hardening nit, not a blocking test-adequacy defect.

finding.summary: New `.catch(() => {})` plus `fonts.check()`'s fallback semantics make the font guard pass vacuously when the webfont stylesheet never loads
finding.evidence: The load pass now swallows every rejection (`document.fonts.load(...).catch(() => {})`, line 374). The comment claims "the check pass below reports as a timeout naming the family", and docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:52-55 repeats that "an unreachable fonts.googleapis.com now reports a clear timeout". Per CSS Font Loading, `document.fonts.check()` returns true when no matching FontFace is registered (the text would render with a fallback), so if index.html's Google Fonts stylesheet fails or is blocked (offline/sandboxed CI), zero Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains faces are registered, every `check(...)` at line 388 returns true immediately, and the follow-up loading poll (line 395) also passes because no face is in `loading`. The harness then screenshots the fallback-serif rendering — precisely the failure this change exists to catch. Before the diff, a rejected `fonts.load()` would have propagated out of `page.evaluate` and failed the run loudly; that detection is now removed. A real assertion would require the family to be present, e.g. checking `[...document.fonts].some(f => f.family === family && f.status === 'loaded')`.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. The finding says the guard consists of a swallowed `fonts.load(...).catch(() => {})` (claimed line 374) followed only by a vacuous `fonts.check()` (claimed line 388) and a "still loading" poll (claimed line 395), and prescribes a per-family `status === 'loaded'` assertion as the missing fix. In the working tree, `pending()` at verify-visual-browser.mjs:415-438 already performs precisely that assertion BEFORE any `check()` call: it maps `[...document.fonts]` filtered by family to their `status` values and reports the family as missing unless `statuses.includes("loaded")` (lines 418-427), with an inline comment explicitly calling out that this is what distinguishes real failure from the "renders with a system fallback" case `check()` reports as success. The per-weight `check()` at line 430 runs only after that gate, so it is not the sole signal, and a family whose faces are all `error`/`unloaded` fails by name. The awaited set is derived from `document.fonts` itself and re-read each poll tick (registry() lines 385-396; loop lines 451-456), failures trigger stylesheet refetch (lines 463-473) and otherwise are recorded in `webFontFailures` for a non-zero exit (lines 488-494) rather than passing. The comment string the finding quotes ("the check pass below reports as a timeout naming the family") does not exist in the source at all — its only occurrence in the repo is inside another agent's report artifact (.agent-review/correctness/stage-detail.json), showing the finding was written against a superseded revision of the file. The cited doc lines also already state the loaded-status pairing (docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:75-76) and record the fully-offline CDN case as a known limitation (lines 89-92).
